newsitem.title: USA: Hein-Werner to sell unit, use proceeds.
newsitem.headline: Hein-Werner to sell unit, use proceeds.

text.p: Hein-Werner Corp said Thursday it agreed to sell for an undisclosed amount of cash, its Winona Van Norman division, which makes engineered machinery to rebuild car and truck engines.

Hein-Werner said sale of the division is part of the company's plan to focus on its core business and to add new business in non-automotive niche markets. The company is a large manufacturer and marketer of collision repair equipment.
Winona Van Norman has experienced lackluster U.S. sales performance and has not rebounded from the weak conditions prevalent during the early 1990s, the company said in a news release.

Hein-Werner said that proceeds from the Winona Van Norman sale and cash from sale of its Great Bend Industries fluid power division strengthens the company's balance sheet and provides flexibility for expansion.

"It gives us the capability to make a non-automotive acquisition in the $40-$50 millon revenue range," said Joseph Dindorf, president and chief executive officer, in a statement. "Our concentration is on companies with good grwoth histories in niche markets which are counter-cyclical to the automotive industry," he said.
Terms of the agreement were not disclosed. The transaction is expected to close in 45 days.
Shares of Hein-Werner were trading off 1/4 to eight. ((Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8787))
